name: secret_needle

question.instructions: Does this log contain a credential or secret (API key, access token, password, private key) anywhere?

criteria.true: a credential or secret value appears somewhere in the log
criteria.false: no credential or secret appears; hashes, ids, UUIDs, checksums, digests and redacted placeholders don't count

notes: needle: one secret line inserted at a random position in a benign ~600-900 token log (GLM writes the haystacks; GLM-written fake secrets are inserted by us); half of all logs also get a credential-looking decoy (hash, UUID, digest, redacted placeholder). Predicted: understudy's max/attention pooling can pick up one salient line and should beat hunch's token mean, which dilutes one line in ~800 tokens. Note: both understudies clip states to 3,000 chars (head 2/3, tail 1/3), so a needle in the middle of a long log can be invisible to them; the lead reads the whole log.
